newsitem.title: USA: MS drug 30-40 pct of AutoImmune spending - Bishop.
newsitem.headline: MS drug 30-40 pct of AutoImmune spending - Bishop.

text.p: AutoImmune Inc president and chief executive officer Robert Bishop said his company's multiple sclerosis drug, Myloral, represented 30 to 40 percent of the Lexington, Mass.-based firm's spending.

The company reported earlier Monday that a 14-center Phase III trial of 500 patients in the United States and Canada of its oral therapy showed there was no difference in response between the treatment and a placebo, and it will put development of Myloral on hold.
The stock fell 9-1/8 to 4-5/8 by early afternoon.
Bishop said in an interview the company's total overall spending was about $80 million and Myloral represented 30 to 40 percent of that sum.
He said the next product in the biotechnology company's product portfolio is Colloral, an oral treatment for rheumatoid arthritis that is nearing completion of three Phase II trials.
"We expect to see preliminary results of the Colloral next month," Bishop said. "And hope to have a Phase III trial underway this summer."
Montogomery Securites analyst David Crossen, said "Colloral cannot be ruled out; I still have hope for it. Less hope than I did."

Bishop's company, which is also developing a medication for diabetes in partnership with Eli Lilly and Co, concentrates on oral products. The other drugs used to treat MS, made by Biogen Inc, Schering-Plough Corp and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd are all administered by injection.
"It's a bit of a shock," Crossen said of the Myloral results. "It raises questions like does oral therapy work and how the placebo effect is so significant."
